01 / From source to sentence

A clearer claim is only the beginning.

Bring the decision memo you are preparing for leadership approval and the sources behind it. See the passage supporting a claim, where your wording goes further, and a proposed revision you can inspect before accepting.

The planned experience keeps that relationship through revisions. When wording or linked evidence changes, the affected check reopens instead of letting an old review stand for a new claim.

Connect Link a claim to a precise passage in your source.

Inspect See what the source supports and what remains uncertain.

Revise Preview and accept a scoped change, with undo.

Recheck Revisit changed claims before sharing your draft.

02 / Built around your judgment

Keep the evidence in view as your writing changes.

A smoother rewrite can quietly become a stronger claim. 🪔 diyalamp’s planned review experience keeps attention on the passages that need another look.

Pull on a claim.

Distinguish an observation from an explanation. See whether the evidence supports what you are saying, and examine a more precise formulation.

A claim proportionate to its support.

A new revision needs a new check.

When checked wording or its linked source changes, the prior check becomes outdated. Inspect the change and decide whether to revise or add evidence.

Visible review status for the current wording.

Inspect the source, not just the verdict.

Read the supporting passage beside the claim. Distinguish supplied evidence from an AI inference, and question the finding yourself.

A review you can examine.

Ask what would change your mind.

Examine the strongest alternative, a pivotal uncertainty, or the evidence that would reverse your recommendation.

A decision that can be reconsidered.

03 / Grow a writing culture

Build a culture of defensible decisions.

Move from one well-reasoned memo to a shared writing practice. Make claims traceable, alternatives visible, and uncertainty explicit across your team.

The long-term vision is an organizational home for writing standards and decision rationale, so teams can understand why a choice was made and when to revisit it.

Rigor should help people think. It should never become a document quota, an employee score, or another approval checklist.

An open foundation

Reasoning you can inspect.

The open-source engine organizes review around framing, evidence, reasoning, alternatives, and an explicit decision. The planned product turns that foundation into a useful writing experience.

AI findings can be wrong. Authors must be able to inspect, challenge, and dismiss them. This approach does not guarantee a correct business outcome.

Explore the open-source engine
What can I use today?

The scripted evidence-and-revision example on this page and the open-source engine. Hosted review, accounts, subscriptions, and team workflows are still in development.

Will 🪔 diyalamp write the decision for me?

The aim is to help you develop and test your reasoning. Proposed edits should be visible, reversible, and accepted by you. The final decision stays yours.

Is this only a document editor?

The initial focus is product decision memos prepared for leadership review. The aim is to keep claims and evidence connected as the draft changes, so a previous check does not silently apply to new wording.

Does defensible mean defending my original position?

No. A strong review can change the recommendation. The goal is a decision proportionate to the evidence, including honest uncertainty and the strongest alternative.

Clear words. Considered decisions.
